request.text: Credential dumping is suspected on WORKSTATION5. Contain the host.

e1.rationale: Outflank-Dumpert.exe was started from cmd.exe, opened lsass.exe with full access and wrote dumpert.dmp: credential dumping on WORKSTATION5. Isolate it now.

author: coding agent (demo fixture)
notes: Demo fixture (plan §E.5, T8.1), not research data. Scenario, context and labels drafted by the coding agent; to be reviewed by the team at R1 sign-off. CHG-DEMO-1 is an approved red-team ticket for rt.operator: in E1-E4 the activity matches it in host, command and time but not in account (wardog); E5 sets the acting user to rt.operator, so the ticket covers every suspicious event. E4 (partial chain) is not in §E.5's list; it exists because the validator requires all seven variants. E3 moves every record that mentions Outflank-Dumpert (image loads, the accesses to it by csrss/cmd/conhost and the prefetch file included), so no trace of the attack stays on WORKSTATION5. Moved records keep the local account's domain (WORKSTATION5\wardog) and the original Message text; move_host changes the host fields only. E2 (seed 7) samples 10, 23 and 116 under the rule adopted before M6 (actor or target in the attack process set, or a file/registry path naming an attack image; record 94, the dumper's prefetch file, flagged at R1, is now excluded by the rule as well); the sampling basis is stored with the E2 case, so later label changes do not move it (make regenerate-e2 recomputes it, logged). In E5 the command is rendered only on record 49 (process creation), so its decisive entry is the ticket on host, account and time plus 49's command line. Labels extended after R1 to every state-changing action on every target of the scenario; those 31 entries were re-decided under rule A (scope rule, team lead decision 13/10/2026): their notes say "decided by rule A, 13/10/2026" or "decided by Claude Code under rule A, please spot-check", with the reason. E3 also accepts draft_report as an escalation (reporting WORKSTATION6, rule A). The scope (WORKSTATION5 and the processes and account acting on it) is authored in "scope".
